answer: Inter-arrival entropy gating. Each identity's first N actions must show human-scale timing variance; agents stamping registrations in lockstep exceed the entropy floor and get throttled to a glacier pace, one action per several minutes. A genuine user's uneven rhythm clears the queue fast while a farm stalls. Attackers must either pay for enough real distinct humans to seed variance, or buy time their mass registration loses at the pearl of viability—every hour of queue delay is sunk cost. Only identities surviving to the zenith of the window gain full throughput rights.
